title: Normalized tensor comparison models preserve flat modules
statement:
variable {C₀ C₁ : Type c} [Category.{v} C₀] [Category.{v} C₁]
  [EssentiallySmall.{max c v r} C₀] [EssentiallySmall.{max c v r} C₁]
  (J₀ : GrothendieckTopology C₀) (J₁ : GrothendieckTopology C₁)
  (R₀ : Sheaf J₀ CommRingCat.{max c v r}) (R₁ : Sheaf J₁ CommRingCat.{max c v r})


theorem tensorComparisonModel_preserves_flat
    (F : Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J₀ R₀ ⥤ Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J₁ R₁)
    [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    (S₀ : Closed.{c, v, r} J₀ R₀) (S₁ : Closed.{c, v, r} J₁ R₁)
    (T₀ : Models.{c, v, r} J₀ R₀ S₀) (T₁ : Models.{c, v, r} J₁ R₁ S₁)
    (μ : S₀.tensor ⋙ F.mapDerivedCategory ≅
      (F.mapDerivedCategory.prod F.mapDerivedCategory) ⋙ S₁.tensor)
    (t : TensorComparisonModel.{c, v, r} J₀ J₁ R₀ R₁ F S₀ S₁ T₀ T₁ μ)
    (M : Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J₀ R₀)
    (hM : SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite (J := J₀) (R := R₀) M) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite (J := J₁) (R := R₁) (F.obj M)

proof.text: For a flat sheaf module M, take the cochain complex P with M in degree zero and zero elsewhere. Identify its degree-zero term with M and its other terms with zero, so all terms are flat. The bounded-above flat K-flat criterion makes P K-flat, and TensorComparisonModel.kflat makes F(P) K-flat. Transfer this to native categorical K-flatness by RingedDerivedNative.kFlat and HomotopyCategory.kFlat_quotient_obj_iff. The singleMapHomologicalComplex isomorphism identifies F(P) with the complex concentrated in degree zero at F(M). CochainComplex.kFlat_single_obj_iff_flat makes F(M) categorically flat; siteSheafTensorRightIso transfers exactness of its tensor functor to site tensor flatness. This proves the property of the already constructed F(M), without choosing any object from an existence assertion.
